# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the legacy billing system ("Old System") to the new billing system ("New System"). Both systems will run in parallel throughout the migration, with dual-write/dual-read reconciliation used to validate data integrity before and after each user's cutover. The old system remains fully operational and authoritative-fallback capable until well after the final user batch has been migrated and independently verified.

---

## Phase 1: Canary — 1% of users (~400 users)

**Percentage of users:** 1% (~400 users)

**Entry criterion:** New system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including successful processing of synthetic invoices, refunds, proration, and tax calculation scenarios that mirror production data shapes; on-call rotation, rollback tooling, and reconciliation dashboards are deployed and verified functional; legal/finance sign-off obtained for parallel-run reconciliation approach.

**Cohort selection:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk test customers (non-enterprise, monthly billing cycle, no active disputes or credits).

**Activities:** Migrate account, payment method tokens, and subscription state; run both systems in shadow mode (old system remains system of record); compare invoices/charges generated by both systems for a minimum of one full billing cycle before treating any canary user as "complete."

**Exit criterion to advance:** Zero critical discrepancies between old and new system outputs for the full canary cohort across one billing cycle; error budget and metrics below halt thresholds (see Metrics section).

---

## Phase 2: Early Adoption — 15% of users (~6,000 users)

**Percentage of users:** 15% (~6,000 users, cumulative 16%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by engineering and finance; no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 defects from Phase 1; reconciliation automation (not manual spot-checks) is live and running on a scheduled basis; customer support playbooks and escalation paths for billing discrepancies are published and support team trained.

**Cohort selection:** Broaden to include self-serve customers across all billing cycle types (monthly, annual, usage-based) but exclude enterprise/contract customers with custom billing terms and any customers with an open billing dispute or delinquent balance.

**Activities:** Migrate in daily sub-batches of ~500–800 users rather than a single bulk push; monitor per-batch error rates before proceeding to next sub-batch; maintain dual-run reconciliation for at least 7 days per sub-batch before finalizing cutover for that sub-batch.

**Exit criterion to advance:** Cumulative discrepancy rate remains below halt threshold for the full phase duration; customer support ticket volume related to billing does not exceed 1.5x pre-migration baseline; payment failure/decline rate for migrated cohort is within 0.5 percentage points of the old system's baseline decline rate.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability — 84% of users (~33,600 users)

**Percentage of users:** 84% (remaining users, cumulative 100%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met; reconciliation false-positive/false-negative rate characterized and understood (so alerts are trustworthy at scale); infrastructure load-tested for full-volume concurrent dual-write throughput; enterprise/contract customer billing logic (custom pricing, multi-entity invoicing, negotiated terms) explicitly validated in staging since these were excluded from Phases 1–2; rollback runbook rehearsed at least once via game-day exercise.

**Cohort selection:** All remaining users, sequenced in weekly waves (e.g., 8–10 waves) rather than a single cutover, with enterprise/contract customers migrated in the final waves of this phase after all self-serve segments succeed, and with each enterprise account individually verified post-migration before being marked complete.

**Activities:** Continue dual-run reconciliation per wave for a minimum of one full billing cycle per wave; maintain old system as fully operational fallback with real-time failback capability for any migrated user throughout this phase and for a defined post-migration soak period afterward.

**Exit criterion to complete rollout:** All waves migrated with discrepancy and support-ticket metrics within threshold; final reconciliation sign-off from finance confirming that a full billing cycle's worth of revenue reconciles between old and new systems for the entire user base.

---

## Post-Migration Soak & Decommission (Separate Phase — Not a Migration Batch)

**Note:** Per requirements, decommissioning the old system is explicitly *not* part of Phase 3 or any user-migration batch. This is a distinct, subsequent phase that begins only after Phase 3's exit criteria are met.

**Entry criterion:** 100% of users migrated and stable in the new system for a minimum soak period of two full consecutive billing cycles with no reopened reconciliation discrepancies; finance has completed a full audit reconciling both systems' historical records; old system has been placed in read-only archival mode (not yet deleted) for a minimum of one additional billing cycle beyond the soak period; data retention/compliance requirements for financial records confirmed satisfied by an accessible archive independent of the live old system.

**Activities:** Transition old system to read-only archive; retain archived data per regulatory retention requirements (e.g., 7 years for financial records, subject to jurisdiction); only after archive is confirmed complete and independently accessible does infrastructure decommissioning of the old system begin.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges during dual-run reconciliation due to timing differences between systems | Implement idempotency keys across both systems and run automated reconciliation jobs comparing transaction ledgers hourly during migration, with automatic quarantine of mismatched records | Engineering Lead (Billing Platform)
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing declined charges for affected customers | Pre-validate tokenization compatibility with payment processor in staging for 100% of card network/processor combinations before Phase 1, and run a token-validation dry run against a copy of production tokens | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms or multi-entity billing are migrated before their custom logic is fully supported, causing invoice errors | Explicitly exclude enterprise/custom-contract accounts from Phases 1–2, require dedicated validation and account-by-account sign-off before including them in Phase 3, and assign a customer success owner per enterprise account during their migration wave | VP of Customer Success
RISK: Rollback from new system back to old system is not exercised in practice and fails when actually needed | Conduct a scheduled rollback game-day/rehearsal before Phase 3 entry, and require documented, tested rollback runbooks with defined RTO before any phase begins | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during migration, delaying detection of systemic issues | Establish a dedicated migration support queue with tagged tickets, staff surge coverage during each migration wave, and require ticket-volume metrics to feed directly into the halt-decision dashboard | Head of Customer Support
RISK: Regulatory or tax calculation differences between old and new systems cause compliance exposure (e.g., incorrect sales tax/VAT) | Run parallel tax calculation comparison for every invoice during dual-run period and require finance/tax team sign-off before any cohort's charges are considered final in the new system | Finance/Tax Compliance Owner

---

## Metrics and Halt Conditions

The rollout will be automatically paused (no further batches promoted or new cohorts started) and escalated to the incident commander if any of the following thresholds are breached for any active cohort:

- **Billing discrepancy rate > 0.1%** of transactions in a given batch/wave (comparing old vs. new system output) within any rolling 24-hour window — HALT rollout, do not proceed to next batch until root-caused and resolved.
- **Payment failure/decline rate increase of more than 1.0 percentage point** relative to the old system's baseline for the same cohort — HALT and investigate.
- **Reconciliation job failure or lag exceeding 4 hours** (jobs not completing or falling behind real-time processing) — HALT until reconciliation pipeline health is restored.
- **Critical (Sev-1) incident count ≥ 1** attributable to the new billing system in a 24-hour period — HALT immediately pending post-incident review.

---

PHASES: 3
